description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs:75-80

SIGNATURE:
    /// Returns true if this account supports the given JMAP object type.
    ///
    /// Called by the server consumer (e.g. the session capability
    /// builder) — NOT called internally by the handler library.
    /// Backends that support all types unconditionally can return
    /// `true` always.
    fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool;

PROBLEM:
The doc says "Returns true if this account supports the given JMAP
object type" — but the signature has no `account_id` or `caller`
parameter. The answer cannot in fact depend on the account or the
caller; the doc misnames it.

Backends that need to make this answer per-account (e.g., multi-tenant
SaaS where some tenants have contacts disabled, or where contacts is a
paid feature) cannot implement that policy through this trait. They
must either:
(a) Lie — return true for everyone and rely on a later access-control
    check in create_object/destroy_object, with no session-capability
    signal to the client; or
(b) Wrap the backend in account-specific instances and dispatch per
    request — defeating the cheap-Arc-clone design of the handler
    registration path.

The doc says "Called by the server consumer (e.g. the session
capability builder)" — but session capabilities are advertised to a
specific user with a specific Bearer token, so the answer IS naturally
caller-scoped. The current signature forecloses that.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That a session capability advertisement for one user matches what
  another user would see.
- That changes to the answer (feature flag flip) propagate to existing
  sessions without re-registering handlers.

ASSESSMENT:
P3 because (a) the canonical sibling jmap-mail-server has the same
shape (workspace cookie-cutter), so any fix is a cross-extension
propagation, and (b) most real backends do support all types per
account so the global answer is usually correct. But the doc misleads
implementors about what is and is not parameterizable.

RECOMMENDED:
(a) Reword the doc to match what the signature actually says:
    "Returns true if this backend implementation supports the given
    JMAP object type. The answer is global per backend instance; it
    cannot depend on the account or caller. Consumers needing per-
    account feature gating must wrap the backend or implement gating
    at the session-capability-builder layer."
or
(b) Add `account_id: &Id, caller: &Self::CallerCtx` parameters and
    make it `impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send`
    so backends can consult storage. Propagate to canonical and
    siblings.

Option (a) is the cheap fix; option (b) is the right long-term shape
but is a workspace-wide change.
title: ContactsBackend::supports_type<O> is sync with no caller/account params — implied global-per-process answer is not documented
